per_call_isolated_function_check.note: Direct comparison of greedy_set_utility (reference) vs greedy_set_utility_optimized (E dispatch) on the REAL first Weather_96 training batch, t=0, empty prefix, run through the actual production dispatcher (not a standalone script).

opt03_carryover_real_data.note: OPT03 validated dense_utility_optimized itself (unchanged in OPT04) at 100% non-tie agreement, H96 (500q) and H720 (300q), free-running (no gradient) eval mode.

CRITICAL_FINDING: Per-call agreement (~1e-6 max diff, 0-1 near-ties per thousands of checks, matching OPT02/OPT03) does NOT survive intact through real multi-step ON-POLICY training. Over 10 real optimizer steps (Weather_96, greedy_set, onpolicy, cosine), reference and optimized runs -- started from an IDENTICAL initial state, same batches, same seed -- diverge to only 48.3% selection agreement and a non-bit-exact final model state (param L2 diff 0.233). Root-caused (see research/TRACK-A-WEATHER-OPT04.md section on anomalies): at t=0 on the untouched initial model, oracle target VALUES agree to ~1e-6 and the CE target LABEL (argmax) agrees on every one of 32 rows for a single channel (verified directly) -- so the wiring itself is correct. Across the Weather dataset's 21 channels x K=10 steps x batch, however, a rare fraction of near-ties DO flip the discontinuous argmax CE label between reference and optimized (a ~1e-6 utility difference is enough to flip a label that sits within ~1e-6 of a true tie), each flip perturbing that gradient step by a non-negligible amount. Because prefix_policy=onpolicy feeds the MODEL's own (now perturbed) argmax back into the next step's state, this is a chaotic/butterfly-effect amplification, not a bug: both trajectories are individually valid continuations of the same Oracle definition, but they are NOT the same trajectory once a single label flips.
verdict: CONDITIONAL -- per-call and short free-running numerical equivalence are both fully confirmed (matches OPT02/OPT03). Bit-for-bit (or even close) TRAINING REPRODUCIBILITY under onpolicy multi-step training is NOT preserved -- this is reported as the headline anomaly of OPT04, not hidden, and directly informs the E adoption decision below.
